work_package: B6-FFAP-SEEDS (wave 2) for steps 0 to 3.2 and B7-FFAP-FEATURES (wave 3) for steps 3.3 and 4; algorithm.rs, this manifest and the support document passed from B6 to B7
scope: FEATUREFINDER/FeatureFinderAlgorithmPicked.h/.cpp end to end: getDefaultParameters, updateMembers_ and the run_ parameter reads, the input checks of run, steps 0 to 3.2 (intensity quantiles and scores, trace scores and local maxima, isotope-pattern precalculation, pattern scores, overall scores and seed selection), positionScore_, nearest_, findIsotope_, isotopeScore_, both intensityScore_ overloads and getIsotopeDistribution_; and steps 3.3 and 4 (findBestIsotopeFit_, extendMassTraces_, extendMassTrace_, chooseTraceFitter_, cropFeature_, checkFeatureQuality_, feature creation, the parallel seed loop with its containment pass, intersection_, the overlap resolution, the apex annotation and the abort counts). run produces features end to end. Not ported: writeFeatureDebugInfo_ and abort_reasons_, both reachable only through write_debug, which is refused; the FeatureFinderDefs struct.
method: Port with executed differential tests. The C2 class-level driver ffap_stages and a B6 driver seed_stage run FeatureFinderAlgorithmPicked::run in the product SDK and read its protected seed-stage state through a derived probe class. ../oracle/b6-ffap-seeds/extract.py converts their records into TSV fixtures with floats as IEEE-754 bit patterns; tests/feature_finder_picked_seeds.rs rebuilds every configuration with the Rust loaders and compares members, quantiles, isotope windows, all per-peak score arrays and the ordered seed lists bit for bit. The executed FeatureFinderCentroided -write_ini output (C1) pins the defaults. For the feature stage, ../oracle/b7-ffap-features/extract.py converts the same C2 driver's final FeatureMap, aborts_ map and per-seed replay records into TSV fixtures with floats as IEEE-754 bit patterns; tests/feature_finder_picked.rs runs the algorithm on each configuration and additionally replays step 3.3 seed by seed through the public extension and fitting functions. No C++ runs in the B7 extraction.
evidence_tier: tier 1 (executed differential, product SDK): default parameters (C1 -write_ini), effective members, intensity bins and quantiles, isotope windows (bit for bit, closing B2's pending FFC_1 window comparison), every per-peak trace, intensity, local-maximum and pattern score, overall scores (bit for bit except 99 of 30,840 that the oracle's Apple powf misrounds, where the port asserts the correctly rounded value), printed seed counts, and min_spectra 1 behaviour, over 7 configurations; adapted: the ordered seed lists (source selection code replayed on the library arrays; counts equal the library's printed lines); tier 3: FeatureFinderAlgorithmPicked_test constructor and destructor sections, source-order input checks, parameter conversions and refusals; tier 4: hand-derived scoring cases, area-iterator equivalence, limits; tier 1 for the feature stage: the library's final FeatureMap (counts, charges, labels, num_of_datapoints, hull counts and hull point order exactly; coordinates, intensities, qualities, widths and scores within 1e-9 relative), its aborts_ map and its two std::cout lines, over six configurations; adapted: the per-seed intermediate state of the driver's replay; tier 3: all four FeatureFinderAlgorithmPicked_test sections, including the run() and [EXTRA] #9247 literals; tier 4: intersection_ cases, the cropping position rules, the empty-pattern refusal, the seed-loop ceilings and the thread-count determinism

oracle.comparison: Exact: every f64 and f32 value bit for bit, every count and index equal, on Linux x86-64 against the macOS arm64 oracle. The single exception is the overall score (source std::pow(float, float), Apple powf in the oracle): 99 of 30,840 executed values are one binary32 step away from the correctly rounded power; overall_rounding.tsv lists them and the test requires the port's value to be the correctly rounded one there and the executed one everywhere else. The port evaluates the power as libm::pow in f64 rounded once to f32, which is platform-independent; libm::powf differed from the oracle on 226 of 3,084 FFC_1 scores. Inputs use only IEEE +, -, *, /, sqrt and comparisons besides that power, so no other libm result enters.

target_verification.known_gap: Seeds 11 and 12 of classtest_9247_tight_pattern fit identical traces whose fitted parameters depart from the executed Eigen by up to 2.25e-3 (area) on Linux and 5.81e-4 on macOS arm64. Their fit inputs are bit-identical to the executed ones, so the cause is the Levenberg-Marquardt transcription (docs/TRACE_FITTER_SUPPORT.md, 'Known gap: solver fidelity beyond the fixtures'; lane B3b). Both seeds are rejected by checkFeatureQuality_ in C++ and here with the same reason, so no feature changes. Every other compared value stays within 6.46e-10 on both platforms, and 3,765 of 4,649 are bit-identical.
